## Types

### Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// hide the default console server info on app startup
	HideStartBanner bool

	// optional default values for the console flags
	DefaultDev           bool
	DefaultDataDir       string // if not set, it will fallback to "./pb_data"
	DefaultEncryptionEnv string
	DefaultQueryTimeout  time.Duration // default to core.DefaultQueryTimeout (in seconds)

	// optional DB configurations
	DataMaxOpenConns int                // default to core.DefaultDataMaxOpenConns
	DataMaxIdleConns int                // default to core.DefaultDataMaxIdleConns
	AuxMaxOpenConns  int                // default to core.DefaultAuxMaxOpenConns
	AuxMaxIdleConns  int                // default to core.DefaultAuxMaxIdleConns
	DBConnect        core.DBConnectFunc // default to core.dbConnect
}
```

Config is the PocketBase initialization config struct.

### PocketBase

```go
type PocketBase struct {
	core.App

	// RootCmd is the main console command
	RootCmd *cobra.Command
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

PocketBase defines a PocketBase app launcher.

It implements [core.App](/ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core#App) via embedding and all of the app interface methods could be accessed directly through the instance (eg. PocketBase.DataDir()).

### New

```go
func New() *PocketBase
```

New creates a new PocketBase instance with the default configuration. Use [NewWithConfig](#newwithconfig) if you want to provide a custom configuration.

Note that the application will not be initialized/bootstrapped yet, aka. DB connections, migrations, app settings, etc. will not be accessible. Everything will be initialized when [PocketBase.Start](#pocketbasestart) is executed. If you want to initialize the application before calling [PocketBase.Start](#pocketbasestart), then you'll have to manually call \[PocketBase.Bootstrap].

### NewWithConfig

```go
func NewWithConfig(config Config) *PocketBase
```

NewWithConfig creates a new PocketBase instance with the provided config.

Note that the application will not be initialized/bootstrapped yet, aka. DB connections, migrations, app settings, etc. will not be accessible. Everything will be initialized when [PocketBase.Start](#pocketbasestart) is executed. If you want to initialize the application before calling [PocketBase.Start](#pocketbasestart), then you'll have to manually call \[PocketBase.Bootstrap].

### PocketBase.Execute

```go
func (pb *PocketBase) Execute() error
```

Execute initializes the application (if not already) and executes the pb.RootCmd with graceful shutdown support.

This method differs from pb.Start() by not registering the default system commands!

### PocketBase.Start

```go
func (pb *PocketBase) Start() error
```

Start starts the application, aka. registers the default system commands (serve, superuser, version) and executes pb.RootCmd.
